scope: Repairs only primary latency authority, within-budget feasibility semantics, and global execution order. Task set, B/R/C construction, time budgets, frontier proper-superset rule, acquisition firewall, and claim ceiling are unchanged.

primary_latency.authority: external monotonic wall-clock elapsed time around the measured request
primary_latency.start_boundary: immediately before the client/recorder submits the complete measured request to the HTTP transport
primary_latency.stop_boundary: immediately after the complete measured response body has been received by the client/recorder, before grading or post-processing
primary_latency.required_precision: preserve native monotonic-clock resolution; report at least milliseconds when available
primary_latency.backend_timing_fields: secondary literal measurements only; they do not adjudicate feasibility

task_feasibility.rule: For condition X, task q is feasible at tau iff all three constituted replicates are admissible, all three exact-byte grades are SUCCESS=1, and every replicate has L_primary <= tau.
task_feasibility.reason: The terminal language is reliable practical feasibility within the frozen budget; median-only latency would permit one constituted replicate to exceed the budget.

execution_schedule.authority: complete outcome-independent global order for all 108 measured observations

frontier_logic.F_X: set of primary tasks feasible under condition X at tau
frontier_logic.runtime_positive: F_B(tau) is a proper subset of F_R(tau)
frontier_logic.candidate_positive: F_R(tau) is a proper subset of F_C(tau)
frontier_logic.candidate_terminal: FIXED_SUBSTRATE_EFFECTIVE_CAPABILITY_FRONTIER_SHIFT_OBSERVED iff candidate_positive holds at at least one frozen tau; otherwise NOT_OBSERVED after complete admissible execution
frontier_logic.mixed_outcomes: Preserve all task-level crossings and raw Q/L/W/T/M/F axes regardless of terminal.
